**Verdict: ACCEPT.** I found no concrete blocker. Approval of `ffb402db` did not carry over to this commit; I checked it from scratch, by reading files only.

## The two runtime changes

I compared lines 52–137 of the old copy (`boundary-hardening/evolution-native-before.ts`) against the current `browser/src/source/evolution-native.ts`, and only lines 61 and 137 differ. The old copy's hash (`3d240d1d…`) matches the source pinned by the earlier review in `opus-ffb402db/manifest.json`, `validation.json` and `before-summary.json`. For lines 1–51 I relied on `changes.patch`, which has no hunks there, rather than reading them side by side.

**1. Held-item map without a prototype** (`evolution-native.ts:61`)
- **Before:** `items={}`. Looking up `data.items['constructor' | 'toString' | '__proto__']` returned a truthy inherited `Object.prototype` member. So `held` passed the check at `:107`, `held.holdEffect` was `undefined` (no Everstone), and Cyndaquil at level 14 matched row 0. The old source really returns `eligible`, which matches `before-summary.json` (actual `eligible`, expected `unsupported`).
- **After:** with `Object.create(null)` there is no inherited member and no `__proto__` accessor, so all three keys return `undefined` and the result is `unsupported(['held-item'])`. The test also checks `Object.getPrototypeOf(data.items)===null` on the parsed, frozen object, so it inspects the real data, not just the outcome.
- **No regression from the map change:**
  - Item keys have to match `/^ITEM_\w+$/` (`:63`), so the duplicate check `items[row.item]` could never hit an inherited name. Valid rows are admitted and rejected exactly as before.
  - `items.ITEM_NONE?.…` (`:66`), `Object.freeze`, and the direct reads (`data.items.ITEM_EVERSTONE`, test `:110`) all work the same on a prototype-less object.
  - Only `evolution-native.ts` and its test reference `NativeEvolutionData` or this module, so nothing else relies on `data.items` having a prototype.
- **Basis for "unsupported":** this is the same boundary the code already had for `ITEM_NOT_EXPORTED` (test `:43`). Native `GetMonEvolution` gets a held-item ID plus its hold effect. A name that isn't an exported item has no source ID or effect, so returning unsupported is honest and doesn't invent anything. Native behaviour is unchanged.

**2. Level-up wrapper context** (`evolution-native.ts:137`)
- **Before:** in `{kind:'levelup',...environment}`, `environment.kind:'trade'` came last and overrode `'levelup'`. Kadabra's table then went through the trade branch (`:130`, method 5) and returned 65, matching `before-summary.json` (actual 65, expected 0).
- **After:** `{...environment,kind:'levelup'}`. Kadabra has no level-up rule, so it returns `ineligible` with target 0. The explicit `selectNativeEvolution(...,{kind:'trade'})` call still returns 65, which is the correct positive control.
- **No regression for valid environments:** a typed `NativeEvolutionEnvironment` carries only `night` and `evolutionLocation`, so the merged object is identical. Spreading `undefined` or `{}` is the same as before, and the night/location checks still return unsupported at the same points.
  - In C the caller passes the context (`EVOCTX_LEVELUP`) as an argument, so making the wrapper own the discriminator is the faithful version.
  - The differential test (`test.ts:121`) calls `selectNativeEvolution` directly, so this wrapper change can't affect the oracle results.

## Tests, data and docs
- Both new controls are real negative controls: from the code above, both fail on the old source and pass on the new, which matches the before summary and `after.log` (13/13 pass).
- Pinning the corpus at exactly 9,359 (`test.ts:117`) is stricter than the old `>4000`, and the logged count agrees.
- After the change, `after.log:4` still shows all 26 methods observed and seven function hashes. Those hashes are identical to the ones in `validation-hardening.json`, and the data and C file hashes there match the outer manifest.
- The README addition puts excluding Egg subjects on the native caller and adds no guard to the predicate. That is accurate: `mon.isEgg` is never read in `selectNativeEvolution`.
- The patch touches no Main, Battle, World, VM, State or Mon code, and nothing about item consumption, Shedinja or presentation.

## Verification limits
- I ran nothing: no tests, no `tsc`, no hashing. Every pass/fail result above is my reading of the code, cross-checked against the logs you supplied, not something I reproduced.
- I couldn't decompress `before.log.gz`. The before results rely on `before-summary.json`, backed by my own trace of the old source.
- I didn't re-read the original C for this pass. Neither change alters any native comparison, and the earlier C mapping stands as a separate review.
- This approves only this predicate hardening. It is not approval for an all-methods scene or campaign, or for anything involving the browser, audio, DS storage or hardware.
